Young adult novels, by publication year.The Outsiders: S. E. Hinton wrote it as a teenager and published at 17, using her initials to hide that she was a girl.
Judy Blume's frank story about puberty and religion is often challenged by schools and libraries.
Young adult novels, by publication year.Bridge to Terabithia: Katherine Paterson was inspired by the death of her son's friend, and it won the Newbery Medal.
Young adult novels, by publication year.Hatchet: It follows a boy who survives alone in the wilderness after a plane crash; the author drew on his own outdoor experiences.
Young adult novels, by publication year.Perks of Being a Wallflower: Stephen Chbosky told it in letters, then directed the film himself in 2012.
Young adult novels, by publication year.Twilight: Stephenie Meyer says the vampire love story came to her in a dream.
Young adult novels, by publication year.The Hunger Games: Suzanne Collins was inspired by flipping between reality TV and war coverage, and by the Greek myth of Theseus.
Young adult novels, by publication year.Divergent: Veronica Roth wrote it while still a university student at Northwestern.
Young adult novels, by publication year.The Fault in Our Stars: John Green's title comes from Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, where the fault lies not in our stars.
Young adult novels, by publication year.The Hate U Give: Angie Thomas took the title from Tupac Shakur's phrase, The Hate U Give Little Infants F***s Everybody.

Odd things sent to space.Smuggled corned beef sandwich: An astronaut smuggled a corned beef sandwich aboard Gemini 3, and it crumbled, and NASA was not pleased.
Odd things sent to space.Fallen Astronaut statuette: The Fallen Astronaut is a small aluminum statue left on the Moon by Apollo 15 crew, honoring astronauts who had died.
Odd things sent to space.Voyager Golden Record: The Golden Records carry sounds and images of Earth, including greetings in 55 languages, meant for any alien who might find them.
Odd things sent to space.Pizza Hut pizza to the ISS: Pizza Hut sent a pizza to the ISS in a Russian-promoted deal, the first pizza delivered into space.
Odd things sent to space.Clyde Tombaugh's ashes: The ashes of Clyde Tombaugh, who discovered Pluto, are on New Horizons, which flew past Pluto in 2015.
Odd things sent to space.Luke's lightsaber prop: A prop lightsaber from Star Wars went to the ISS, and Luke's lightsaber was returned to Earth after its stay.
Odd things sent to space.Buzz Lightyear figure: A Buzz Lightyear toy spent about 15 months on the ISS, and flew 'to infinity and beyond' before returning home.
Odd things sent to space.LEGO figures on Juno: Juno carried three LEGO figures: Galileo, Jupiter and Juno, to Jupiter, made of aluminum to withstand space.
Odd things sent to space.Hadfield's Space Oddity video: Chris Hadfield, a Canadian astronaut, recorded a cover of David Bowie's 'Space Oddity' on the ISS, and it went viral.
Odd things sent to space.Tesla Roadster: SpaceX launched Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster on the Falcon Heavy's first flight, with a mannequin called Starman at the wheel.

How many people? From a jury to a megaci.A US trial jury: Twelve jurors comes from English common law, a tradition older than the US, though some states use fewer for civil trials.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.Mayflower passengers: About half were Separatists, the Pilgrims, and the rest were so-called Strangers, hired or traveling for other reasons.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.Residents of Vatican City: It is the world's smallest country, at less than half a square kilometer, and it still has its own army, the Swiss Guard.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.Aboard the Titanic: There were lifeboats for only about 1,178 people, roughly half of those aboard, and many left half empty.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.Madison Square Garden crowd: It is nicknamed the World's Most Famous Arena, and the current building is the fourth to carry the name.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.Wembley Stadium crowd: It is one of Europe's largest stadiums, and the current building replaced the old one in 2007, with an arch visible across London.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.1963 March on Washington: Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his I Have a Dream speech to this crowd in front of the Lincoln Memorial.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.Woodstock 1969: It was held at Max Yasgur's farm in Bethel, New York, and was meant to attract 50,000 but drew roughly eight times as many.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.Rod Stewart, Copacabana 1994: Rod Stewart's free New Year's Eve concert there is among the largest ever, and it was held on the Copacabana beach in Rio.
How many people? From a jury to a megaci.Greater Tokyo: The metropolitan area has about as many people as Poland, in an urban area many times denser than anywhere in Europe.

First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 247: The first modern airliner: all-metal, twin-engined, with retractable landing gear. It carried just ten passengers, yet outflew most rivals of 1933.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 307 Stratoliner: First pressurized airliner in service, it climbed above much of the weather, so passengers in the late 1930s got smoother, quieter flights.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 377 Stratocruiser: A double-decker luxury liner with a lower-deck lounge and bar, descended from a military transport. Its piston engines were notoriously troublesome.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 707: The plane that began the jet age for American airlines. Pan Am's 1958 transatlantic service cut the crossing to about eight hours.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 727: This three-engine jet had a rear airstair, which D. B. Cooper used in 1971 to parachute away with ransom money over the Pacific Northwest.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 747: The upper-deck hump was designed so the nose could swing open for cargo if passengers faded. Nicknamed the Queen of the Skies.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 767: In 1983 an Air Canada 767 ran out of fuel mid-flight, glided down and landed safely at a former airfield in Gimli, Manitoba.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 757: Designed alongside the 767 and sharing its cockpit, so one pilot rating covered both. Its powerful engines let it take off from short runways.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 777: The first Boeing airliner designed entirely on computer, and still the largest twin-engine jet ever flown.
First flights of Boeing airliners.Boeing 787: The Dreamliner's fuselage is mostly carbon-fiber composite, and its large windows dim electronically instead of using pull-down shades.

How long these last.Blink: We blink roughly 15 times a minute, and each blink is so brief that we do not notice the momentary darkness.
How long these last.Proper hand-wash: Ignaz Semmelweis showed in 1847 that handwashing cut deaths in a Vienna maternity ward, though doctors rejected the idea for years.
How long these last.Microwave popcorn: Percy Spencer tested popcorn first when inventing the microwave oven, and then an egg, which exploded in a colleague's face.
How long these last.Sitcom episode (no ads): The format allows around eight minutes of ads in a half-hour slot, leaving about 22 minutes for the show.
How long these last.Feature film: Gone with the Wind ran nearly four hours with an intermission, one of the longest of the major Hollywood hits.
How long these last.A good night's sleep: A night's sleep is made of cycles lasting about 90 minutes each, which is why waking mid-cycle feels groggy.
How long these last.Weekend: Henry Ford adopted the five-day work week in 1926, which helped create the weekend as we know it.
How long these last.Two-week vacation: The US is the only major economy without legally required paid vacation, while many countries mandate four weeks or more.
How long these last.Human pregnancy: The 40 weeks is counted from the last menstrual period, so conception actually occurs around week two.
How long these last.Gap between Summer Olympics: The Greeks called the four-year gap an Olympiad, and used it as a way of dating events across their city-states.

Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Pompeii: Buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, it kept its streets, shops and even wall graffiti frozen in ash.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Carthage: Rome's great rival in the Punic Wars, whose general Hannibal crossed the Alps; Cato ended speeches by demanding it be destroyed.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Lugdunum (Lyon): Capital of Roman Gaul and birthplace of Emperor Claudius, it stands where the Rhône and Saône meet.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Athens: Rome conquered Greece but admired Athens, and Emperor Hadrian adorned it with new buildings and a library.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Londinium (London): A Roman amphitheatre was found under the Guildhall in 1988, a few streets from where this Roman city once stood.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Alexandria: Home to the Pharos lighthouse and a great library, and Rome relied on Egyptian grain shipped through its port.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Antioch: The empire's third-largest city, where Jesus's followers were first called Christians, according to the Acts of the Apostles.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Jerusalem: Titus destroyed it in AD 70, and the Arch of Titus in Rome still shows soldiers carrying away the Temple's treasures.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Babylon: By Roman times the once-great Mesopotamian capital was largely ruins, but Emperor Trajan visited it in AD 116.
Ancient cities by straight-line distance.Persepolis: The ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire was burned by Alexander the Great in 330 BC, and its ruins still stand.

Modern paintings, by date.Liberty Leading the People: Delacroix painted the July Revolution, with Liberty striding forward bare-chested, holding the tricolor.
Modern paintings, by date.Olympia: Manet's nude caused a scandal at the 1865 Salon for its direct stare.
Modern paintings, by date.Impression, Sunrise: Monet's harbor view gave Impressionism its name, after a critic mocked it.
Modern paintings, by date.Luncheon of the Boating Party: Renoir's party scene includes his future wife, Aline Charigot.
Modern paintings, by date.The Starry Night: Van Gogh painted it from his asylum window at Saint-Rémy, though the village is imagined.
Modern paintings, by date.The Scream: Munch made several versions of it, and one was stolen from Oslo in 2004 and later recovered.
Modern paintings, by date.Les Demoiselles d'Avignon: Picasso's painting of five women foreshadowed Cubism.
Modern paintings, by date.American Gothic: Grant Wood used his dentist and his sister as models for the farmer and his daughter.
Modern paintings, by date.The Persistence of Memory: Dalí's melting clocks hang in a small canvas of about 24 by 33 centimeters at MoMA.
Modern paintings, by date.Nighthawks: Hopper's diner scene was inspired by a spot in Greenwich Village.

Elements named after places, by atomic n.Scandium: Named for Scandinavia, it was predicted by Mendeleev as ekaboron.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Gallium: It melts at about 30 degrees Celsius, so it turns liquid in your hand, and its name is Latin for France.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Germanium: Named by Clemens Winkler for Germany, it was another Mendeleev prediction, and it was used in early transistors.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Strontium: It is named for Strontian, a Scottish village, and it gives fireworks a red color.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Polonium: Marie Curie named it for Poland, her homeland, then partitioned; it was the first element she discovered.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Francium: Marguerite Perey found it, and it is so rare and radioactive that fewer than 30 grams exist at a time in Earth's crust.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Americium: Used in smoke detectors, it was named for the Americas, by analogy with europium.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Californium: Made at UC Berkeley and named for the university and the state, it is used in neutron sources.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Nihonium: Discovered in Japan by RIKEN, it was the first element named in Asia, from Nihon.
Elements named after places, by atomic n.Tennessine: Named for Tennessee, home of Oak Ridge National Laboratory; it is a halogen.

When these writing systems first appeare.Cuneiform: Sumerians pressed wedge shapes into wet clay, first for accounting; the word means 'wedge-shaped'.
When these writing systems first appeare.Linear A: A Minoan script from Crete, still undeciphered, unlike its successor Linear B.
When these writing systems first appeare.Chinese oracle bone script: Used on Shang dynasty bones and turtle shells for divination, it is the ancestor of Chinese characters.
When these writing systems first appeare.Phoenician alphabet: This consonant-only alphabet is the ancestor of Greek, Latin, Hebrew and Arabic, and its first letter meant 'ox'.
When these writing systems first appeare.Greek alphabet: Greeks added vowels by repurposing Phoenician consonants, and 'alphabet' comes from alpha and beta.
When these writing systems first appeare.Brahmi script: The ancestor of nearly all scripts of South and Southeast Asia, famous from Emperor Ashoka's edicts.
When these writing systems first appeare.Runes: The Germanic alphabet is called the futhark, after its first six letters.
When these writing systems first appeare.Ogham: An Irish script of strokes along a stone's edge, found on standing stones in Ireland and Britain.
When these writing systems first appeare.Glagolitic: Created for Old Church Slavonic by the missionary brothers Cyril and Methodius, it influenced later Cyrillic.
When these writing systems first appeare.Hangul: King Sejong introduced it to be easy to learn, and its letter shapes mimic the position of the mouth and tongue.

Taming the American West, in order.Louisiana Purchase: President Jefferson paid about $15 million for roughly 2 million square kilometres, doubling the size of the young country.
Taming the American West, in order.Battle of the Alamo: 'Remember the Alamo!' became a rallying cry; defenders including Davy Crockett died, and Texas won independence weeks later.
Taming the American West, in order.Mexican-American War: It ended in 1848 with Mexico giving up land that became California, Nevada, Utah and more.
Taming the American West, in order.Pony Express begins: Riders raced mail between Missouri and California, but the service lasted only about 18 months before the telegraph replaced it.
Taming the American West, in order.Homestead Act: It offered 160 acres to anyone who farmed the land for five years, and drew hundreds of thousands of settlers west.
Taming the American West, in order.Transcontinental Railroad: The golden spike was driven at Promontory Summit, Utah, cutting a cross-country trip from months to about a week.
Taming the American West, in order.Battle of Little Bighorn: Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors wiped out Custer's force, leading to a US victory later in the larger war.
Taming the American West, in order.Gunfight at the O.K. Corral: The famous shootout in Tombstone, Arizona, lasted about 30 seconds and actually took place in a lot beside the corral.
Taming the American West, in order.Oklahoma Land Rush: Settlers raced in at noon; those who sneaked in early were called 'Sooners', giving Oklahoma its nickname.
Taming the American West, in order.Wounded Knee Massacre: US troops killed hundreds of Lakota in South Dakota; it is often seen as the last major clash of the Indian Wars.

Actors' first time as Superman.Bud Collyer (cartoon voice): Bud Collyer gave Clark a gentle voice and Superman a deep one, creating the voice change used by many actors since.
Actors' first time as Superman.Kirk Alyn: His 1948 serial was the first live-action Superman, and the flying scenes were animated.
Actors' first time as Superman.George Reeves: He played the Man of Steel on 1950s TV, and the show was seen by millions of kids.
Actors' first time as Superman.Christopher Reeve: The poster promised that you will believe a man can fly, and Reeve bulked up for the role.
Actors' first time as Superman.Dean Cain: He played Clark in Lois and Clark, and he had played college football and been signed by an NFL team.
Actors' first time as Superman.Tom Welling: Smallville had a no tights, no flights rule, so Clark did not wear the suit until the finale.
Actors' first time as Superman.Brandon Routh: Years after Superman Returns, he played the Atom in the Arrowverse and briefly appeared as an older Superman.
Actors' first time as Superman.Henry Cavill: In Man of Steel, he had the Zack Snyder look; he is also known as Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher.
Actors' first time as Superman.Tyler Hoechlin: He began the role in the series Supergirl before headlining Superman and Lois in 2021.
Actors' first time as Superman.David Corenswet: He was cast in James Gunn's 2025 reboot, starting a new DC universe.

Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.La Celestina: This 1499 tragicomedy gave Spanish a word: a celestina is a matchmaker or go-between.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.Don Quixote (Part One): Often called the first modern novel, its second part came out in 1615, and Cervantes wrote it as a parody of chivalry tales.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.Ficciones: Jorge Luis Borges's short stories include The Library of Babel, an endless library holding every possible book.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.Pedro Páramo: Juan Rulfo's ghostly novel of the town Comala was so admired that García Márquez said he could recite it from memory.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.Hopscotch: Julio Cortázar's book can be read straight through or in a scrambled order he supplied, so no two readings need match.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.One Hundred Years of Solitude: García Márquez's novel of Macondo has sold tens of millions of copies and helped define magical realism.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.The House of the Spirits: Isabel Allende began it as a letter to her dying grandfather in 1981, and it became her first novel.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.Love in the Time of Cholera: García Márquez based it partly on his parents' long courtship, which lasted decades before the two were allowed to marry.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.Like Water for Chocolate: Laura Esquivel opens every chapter with a recipe, tying the heroine's feelings to what she cooks.
Spanish-language classics, by publicatio.The Shadow of the Wind: Carlos Ruiz Zafón's novel is set in Barcelona and features a Cemetery of Forgotten Books.

iPhone models by release.iPhone 3G: It launched with the App Store in 2008, and the model added faster 3G data and GPS.
iPhone models by release.iPhone 4: It introduced the Retina display and FaceTime video calls, and was dogged by the 'antennagate' reception complaint.
iPhone models by release.iPhone 5c: The candy-colored plastic phone was a short-lived experiment in cheaper iPhones.
iPhone models by release.iPhone 6 Plus: Apple's first big-screen iPhone, at 5.5 inches, drew 'bendgate' complaints about bending in pockets.
iPhone models by release.iPhone SE (1st gen): It packed the iPhone 6s internals into a 4-inch iPhone 5s body at $399.
iPhone models by release.iPhone X: Dropping the home button, it introduced Face ID and a notched OLED display, marking ten years since the original iPhone.
iPhone models by release.iPhone XR: This colorful LCD model was widely reported as the best-selling iPhone of 2019.
iPhone models by release.iPhone 12 mini: The smallest modern flagship, its weak sales led Apple to end the mini line after the next model.
iPhone models by release.iPhone 14 Pro: It introduced the Dynamic Island, a pill-shaped cutout that changes shape to display alerts.
iPhone models by release.iPhone 16e: Launched in February 2025, this budget model replaced the SE line and debuted Apple's first in-house modem.

Hexadecimal numbers by value.0xF: The 0x prefix marks hexadecimal in many languages, and F is the biggest single digit, standing for 15.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0x1A: A stands for 10 in hex, so 1A is one sixteen plus ten; hex digits let programmers write bytes in just two characters.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0x2F: In the ASCII character table, this value is the slash character, '/', which also separates folders in web addresses.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0x40: A power of two, 2 to the sixth, and in ASCII this value is '@', the symbol at the heart of every email address.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0x64: In ASCII this value is a lowercase 'd', and it is also a tidy way to see that hex 64 equals decimal 100.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0xFF: The largest value in one byte; it means full brightness in a color channel, so #FFFFFF is pure white.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0x100: One more than a byte can hold, so adding 1 to 0xFF is the classic overflow, as in the old 8-bit games.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0x3E8: Hex is awkward for round decimals, so a plain one thousand looks odd as 3E8, though it is easy to check by hand.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0xBEEF: Programmers love hex words, like 0xDEADBEEF as a debug marker and 0xCAFEBABE at the start of Java class files.
Hexadecimal numbers by value.0xFFFF: The largest 16-bit unsigned number, and also the highest TCP or UDP port number your computer can use.

Musical ensembles by number of players.Solo: Bach's cello suites and Paganini's Caprices are famous works for a lone, unaccompanied player.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Duet: Piano duets sometimes seat two players at one keyboard, called playing 'four hands'.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Trio: The classical piano trio, with piano, violin and cello, was a favorite of Beethoven and Schubert.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Quartet: Haydn is called the father of the string quartet: two violins, a viola and a cello.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Quintet: Schubert's Trout Quintet swaps a second violin for a double bass, giving it a deep, unusual sound.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Sextet: Brahms wrote two string sextets, with the extra players doubling the violas and cellos.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Septet: Beethoven's Septet in E-flat was one of his most popular pieces during his lifetime.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Octet: Mendelssohn wrote his famed String Octet at just 16 years old.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Nonet: Rare enough that composers rarely write for it. Louis Spohr's 1813 nonet is a well-known example.
Musical ensembles by number of players.Dectet: Named from the Latin for ten. It is rare enough that groups usually just say 'ten-piece'.

When these famous dishes were created.Pizza Margherita: Raffaele Esposito of Naples supposedly made it in honor of Queen Margherita, with red tomato, white mozzarella and green basil.
When these famous dishes were created.Peach Melba: Auguste Escoffier created it at London's Savoy for the soprano Nellie Melba.
When these famous dishes were created.Waldorf salad: Created at New York's Waldorf Hotel by maitre d' Oscar Tschirky, it combines apples, celery and mayonnaise.
When these famous dishes were created.Caesar salad: Named after chef Caesar Cardini, who made it in Tijuana, Mexico, not after Julius Caesar.
When these famous dishes were created.Philly cheesesteak: Pat Olivieri, a hot dog vendor, supposedly invented it by grilling steak slices in Philadelphia.
When these famous dishes were created.Cobb salad: Made at Hollywood's Brown Derby restaurant, supposedly by Robert Cobb from leftovers.
When these famous dishes were created.Nachos: Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya improvised them for hungry guests at a restaurant in Piedras Negras, Mexico.
When these famous dishes were created.Bananas Foster: Created at Brennan's in New Orleans, and named after a friend of the owner, Richard Foster. It is set alight at the table.
When these famous dishes were created.Hawaiian pizza: Greek-Canadian restaurateur Sam Panopoulos invented it in Ontario, not in Hawaii.
When these famous dishes were created.Buffalo wings: Said to have begun at the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York, as a late-night snack.

Game boards by number of cells.Tic-tac-toe: With perfect play by both sides it always ends in a draw, so the game is considered solved.
Game boards by number of cells.Fifteen puzzle: Sam Loyd popularized it in the 1880s, though half of the possible starting arrangements can't be solved.
Game boards by number of cells.Nine Men's Morris (points): Boards for it were carved into ancient temple roofs, and Shakespeare mentioned it in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
Game boards by number of cells.Connect Four: Computers have solved it: the first player can always force a win with perfect play.
Game boards by number of cells.Rubik's Cube (stickers): It has 54 stickers and over 43 quintillion possible positions; Ernő Rubik invented it in 1974 to teach spatial thinking.
Game boards by number of cells.Chessboard: The checkered pattern came to medieval Europe later; earlier boards were plain.
Game boards by number of cells.Sudoku: Despite its Japanese name, it was developed in the US as 'Number Place' before Japan popularized it.
Game boards by number of cells.Battleship grid: It began as a pencil-and-paper game before Milton Bradley's plastic version in 1967.
Game boards by number of cells.Scrabble board: Alfred Butts invented the game on this 15 by 15 grid during the Great Depression.
Game boards by number of cells.Go board: The number of possible positions exceeds the atoms in the universe, and AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol here in 2016.

Word count of these classic books.The Little Prince (English): Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's tale of a boy from an asteroid is among the most translated books in the world.
Word count of these classic books.Animal Farm: Orwell struggled to find a publisher for his satire of Soviet communism.
Word count of these classic books.Fahrenheit 451: Bradbury wrote the first version in a UCLA library basement on a rented typewriter; the title is the supposed temperature at which paper burns.
Word count of these classic books.The Catcher in the Rye: J.D. Salinger's teen narrator Holden Caulfield made it a favorite of readers, and a frequent target of challenges in schools.
Word count of these classic books.Pride and Prejudice: Jane Austen first wrote it as 'First Impressions' in the 1790s, with its famous opening on single men and fortunes.
Word count of these classic books.Dracula: Bram Stoker told it in letters and diary entries, and drew partly on Vlad the Impaler, though this is debated.
Word count of these classic books.Jane Eyre: Charlotte Brontë published it under the name Currer Bell.
Word count of these classic books.Ulysses: Joyce's novel follows one Dublin day, 16 June 1904, now celebrated as Bloomsday.
Word count of these classic books.Atlas Shrugged: Ayn Rand's novel of striking industrialists includes a radio speech of about 60 pages.
Word count of these classic books.In Search of Lost Time: Proust's seven-volume novel is famous for the madeleine dipped in tea.

Famous tech flops.Apple Lisa: Priced at around 10,000 dollars, Lisa was among the first personal computers with a graphical interface and mouse, but it was too costly to sell well.
Famous tech flops.Apple Newton: This early tablet's handwriting recognition was mocked in a famous Doonesbury strip and The Simpsons, though it influenced later PDAs.
Famous tech flops.Nintendo Virtual Boy: Nintendo's red 3D console made players lean into a headset and gave many headaches; it was discontinued within months.
Famous tech flops.Segway: Inventor Dean Kamen's two-wheeled scooter was hyped as reinventing cities, but it found a niche mostly with tour groups and security guards.
Famous tech flops.Microsoft Zune: Microsoft's answer to the iPod had a brown colorway and lasted only a few years, though its subscription music service foreshadowed streaming.
Famous tech flops.Google Wave: Google's real-time collaboration tool confused many users and was shut down within about a year, though its ideas influenced later products.
Famous tech flops.Google Glass: These smart glasses with a tiny display drew privacy worries and the nickname 'Glassholes', and the consumer version was pulled in 2015.
Famous tech flops.Amazon Fire Phone: Amazon's phone with a 3D-style 'Dynamic Perspective' feature flopped so badly that Amazon wrote down roughly 170 million dollars in unsold stock.
Famous tech flops.Quibi: This short-form streaming service raised nearly 2 billion dollars yet shut down in about six months, reportedly after the pandemic scuttled its mobile-first plan.
Famous tech flops.Humane Ai Pin: The screenless wearable projector pitched as a smartphone replacement drew harsh reviews and was shut down within about a year of shipping.

Search engines by launch.Archie: Archie was created at McGill University in Montreal, and it searched the file names on FTP servers before the web existed.
Search engines by launch.WebCrawler: WebCrawler was the first search engine to index entire pages, not just titles, and it was later bought by AOL.
Search engines by launch.AltaVista: AltaVista was fast and could handle natural-language queries, and was once the leading search engine before Google overtook it.
Search engines by launch.Ask Jeeves: Ask Jeeves invited you to type questions in plain English, and its butler mascot was based on P. G. Wodehouse's valet.
Search engines by launch.Yandex: Yandex is Russia's leading search engine, and its name stands for 'yet another indexer'.
Search engines by launch.Google: Google ranked pages by links to them using PageRank, a method named in part after Larry Page, one of its founders.
Search engines by launch.Baidu: Baidu is China's leading search engine, and its name comes from a Song dynasty poem about searching for a person in a crowd.
Search engines by launch.DuckDuckGo: DuckDuckGo built its brand on privacy, and doesn't track your searches or create profiles of its users.
Search engines by launch.Bing: Microsoft launched Bing as a replacement for Live Search, and its homepage shows daily photographs from around the world.
Search engines by launch.Perplexity: Perplexity answers questions in sentences with citations, and uses large language models to summarize the web.

How old these ancient ruins are.Tower of Jericho: This stone tower, in what is now the West Bank, stood about eight metres high and is among the oldest monumental structures.
How old these ancient ruins are.Ġgantija temples, Malta: On the island of Gozo, these stone temples are older than Stonehenge and the pyramids, and legend credits a giantess.
How old these ancient ruins are.Great Sphinx of Giza: Carved from a limestone outcrop, it probably shows King Khafre's face on a lion's body, and its nose is long missing.
How old these ancient ruins are.Ziggurat of Ur: Built for the moon god Nanna by King Ur-Nammu, this stepped temple tower was partly rebuilt in the 20th century.
How old these ancient ruins are.Abu Simbel: Ramesses II's temple was cut up and moved in the 1960s to save it from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.
How old these ancient ruins are.Great Stupa at Sanchi: Commissioned by Emperor Ashoka, this Buddhist monument has carved gateways showing scenes from the Buddha's earlier lives.
How old these ancient ruins are.Colosseum: It held an estimated 50,000 spectators and opened with games lasting around 100 days.
How old these ancient ruins are.Hōryū-ji, Japan: This temple near Nara is generally considered to contain the oldest wooden buildings in the world.
How old these ancient ruins are.Kailasa Temple, Ellora: The whole temple was carved downward from a single rock face, a feat that took decades.
How old these ancient ruins are.Alhambra palaces: The palace of the Nasrid rulers of Granada has walls and ceilings covered in intricate stucco and carved poetry.

Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Ivan: Ivan wrecked Grenada before hitting the Gulf Coast, and was one of the strongest of its season.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Wilma: It holds the record for the lowest pressure ever measured in an Atlantic hurricane, 882 millibars.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Ike: Its storm surge drowned parts of Galveston, Texas, and the storm was unusually wide.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Irene: It flooded Vermont and the Northeast, far from where most people expect hurricane damage.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Matthew: The first Category 5 Atlantic hurricane in nearly a decade, it devastated Haiti.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Michael: It hit Mexico Beach, Florida, as a Category 5, and was among the strongest US landfalls on record.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Dorian: It stalled over the Bahamas, pounding Grand Bahama and Abaco with Category 5 winds for a day.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Ida: It hit Louisiana on the anniversary of Katrina, and its remnants flooded New York City.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Ian: It hit southwest Florida as a Category 4, flooding Fort Myers, and was one of the costliest ever.
Atlantic hurricanes of recent decades.Hurricane Helene: It caused catastrophic flooding hundreds of kilometres inland in Appalachia, including around Asheville.

War movies by release.All Quiet on the Western Front: Its 1930 screening in Berlin was disrupted by Nazis, who released mice in the cinema; the film won the Best Picture Oscar.
War movies by release.The Bridge on the River Kwai: The real Burma Railway killed thousands of prisoners of war and Asian labourers, far grimmer than the film suggests.
War movies by release.Lawrence of Arabia: David Lean's desert epic was filmed in 70mm, shot partly in Jordan, Morocco and Spain, and it made Peter O'Toole a star.
War movies by release.The Great Escape: It's based on a real 1944 breakout from Stalag Luft III; 76 men escaped and 50 were executed afterward.
War movies by release.Patton: George C. Scott famously refused his Best Actor Oscar for the title role, calling the awards a meat parade.
War movies by release.The Deer Hunter: The Russian roulette scenes have haunted viewers, and Christopher Walken won Best Supporting Actor for his role.
War movies by release.Platoon: Oliver Stone drew on his own Vietnam service for the story, and the film won Best Picture.
War movies by release.Black Hawk Down: Ridley Scott's account of the 1993 Battle of Mogadishu was based on Mark Bowden's book and used real Army helicopter crews.
War movies by release.The Hurt Locker: Kathryn Bigelow became the first woman to win the Best Director Oscar for this bomb-disposal drama.
War movies by release.Hacksaw Ridge: Desmond Doss, a conscientious objector who never carried a gun, saved around 75 men at Okinawa and received the Medal of Honor.

When these chocolate makers got started.Cadbury: Cadbury was started by John Cadbury in Birmingham, and it began by selling cocoa and drinking chocolate before making bars.
When these chocolate makers got started.Lindt: Lindt's founder's son Rodolphe invented conching, a process that made chocolate smooth and creamy.
When these chocolate makers got started.Ghirardelli: Ghirardelli was founded in San Francisco during the Gold Rush, and it's one of the oldest chocolate companies in the US.
When these chocolate makers got started.Hershey's: Milton Hershey made caramels first, and he built a whole town, Hershey, Pennsylvania, around his chocolate factory.
When these chocolate makers got started.Milka: Milka's purple cow is a famed brand mascot, and the Swiss-made chocolate was named after milk and cacao.
When these chocolate makers got started.Toblerone: Toblerone's triangular shape is said to resemble the Matterhorn, and its name mixes the founder's name with the Italian word for nougat.
When these chocolate makers got started.Mars: Mars was founded by Frank Mars, and its Milky Way bar came in 1923 and Snickers was named after a family horse.
When these chocolate makers got started.Godiva: Godiva was founded in Brussels, and its name and logo refer to Lady Godiva, who legendarily rode naked through Coventry.
When these chocolate makers got started.Ferrero: Ferrero is behind Nutella, which was made as a hazelnut spread, as cocoa was scarce after World War II.
When these chocolate makers got started.Kinder Surprise: Kinder Surprise's chocolate eggs hide a small toy, and they're banned in the US because of choking hazards.

Milestones in light and optics.Alhazen's Book of Optics: Ibn al-Haytham argued we see because light enters the eye, not because rays leave it, and tested ideas with experiments.
Milestones in light and optics.Compound microscope: Often credited to the Dutch spectacle-maker Zacharias Janssen and his father.
Milestones in light and optics.Lippershey's telescope: Dutch spectacle-maker Hans Lippershey applied for a patent. Galileo built his own after hearing of it.
Milestones in light and optics.Newton splits light (prism): Newton showed that white light is a mix of colours, using a second prism to recombine them.
Milestones in light and optics.Speed of light measured: Ole Rømer used timings of Jupiter's moon Io to show light has a finite speed.
Milestones in light and optics.Huygens' wave theory: Christiaan Huygens argued light is a wave, in contrast to Newton's particle view.
Milestones in light and optics.Kaleidoscope: Invented by Scottish scientist David Brewster, it sold hundreds of thousands in just a few months.
Milestones in light and optics.Fresnel lens: Lighthouse lenses by Augustin-Jean Fresnel are far lighter than a solid lens of the same power.
Milestones in light and optics.Holography: Dennis Gabor invented it and won the 1971 Nobel Prize; lasers made it practical.
Milestones in light and optics.Low-loss optical fiber: Corning engineers made fibre clear enough for long-distance signals, the foundation of the internet.

Superconductors by critical temperature.Tungsten: Tungsten becomes superconducting only about 15 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero. It also has the highest melting point of any metal.
Superconductors by critical temperature.Aluminium: Aluminium turns superconducting at 1.2 K, near absolute zero. The same metal is used for drinks cans and foil.
Superconductors by critical temperature.Mercury: Mercury was the first superconductor ever found, in 1911 by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes. He saw its resistance suddenly vanish.
Superconductors by critical temperature.Lead: Lead superconducts below 7.2 K. It was one of the early elements studied, and a handy cheap reference in classrooms.
Superconductors by critical temperature.Niobium: Niobium has the highest transition temperature of any pure element at normal pressure. It is used in particle accelerators.
Superconductors by critical temperature.Niobium-tin (Nb₃Sn): This niobium-tin alloy is drawn into wire for powerful magnets, including some in MRI machines and fusion experiments. It is brittle, so it is shaped before being reacted.
Superconductors by critical temperature.Magnesium diboride: Its superconductivity was discovered only in 2001, surprising for such a simple compound. It's cheap, and it superconducts at 39 K.
Superconductors by critical temperature.YBCO cuprate: YBCO was the first material to superconduct above liquid nitrogen's boiling point (77 K) in 1987. That made cooling far cheaper.
Superconductors by critical temperature.BSCCO (Bi-2223) cuprate: Bismuth strontium calcium copper oxide is made into flexible tapes for power cables. It works at temperatures of liquid nitrogen.
Superconductors by critical temperature.Hg-1223 mercury cuprate: This mercury-based ceramic holds the record for the highest transition temperature at normal pressure. It was found in 1993 and remains unbeaten.

How old these food and drink businesses.Sean's Bar, Athlone: This pub claims to be the oldest in Ireland and Guinness World Records has recognised the claim. The walls hold coins and old documents.
How old these food and drink businesses.Weihenstephan brewery: Founded by Benedictine monks in Bavaria, it's often called the world's oldest brewery still operating. It's now owned by the Bavarian state.
How old these food and drink businesses.Antinori wines: The Florentine winemaking family has run its business for over 600 years, through about 26 generations. It's one of Italy's best-known names.
How old these food and drink businesses.Twinings tea: Thomas Twining started in London's Strand, and the company still operates from the same address. It was a coffee house first.
How old these food and drink businesses.Ruinart Champagne: The oldest established champagne house was founded in Reims. Its founder Nicolas Ruinart was a cloth merchant before turning to bubbly.
How old these food and drink businesses.Moët & Chandon: Claude Moët began selling the sparkling wine of Champagne to European courts. The house later added Dom Pérignon to its range.
How old these food and drink businesses.Baker's Chocolate: A doctor and a chocolate maker set up this firm in Massachusetts, in the American colonies. It's one of the oldest American food brands.
How old these food and drink businesses.King Arthur Baking: The Boston firm began importing English flour. It took the name from the Arthurian legend, and remains employee-owned.
How old these food and drink businesses.Pillsbury: Founded in Minneapolis on the power of the falls, this company created the Doughboy, a symbol of baking. Poppin' Fresh debuted in 1965.
How old these food and drink businesses.Smucker's: Jerome Smucker began by pressing apple cider and making apple butter in Ohio. A jam slogan from the family name became famous.

When these universities were founded.Al-Qarawiyyin, Fez: It started with Fatima al-Fihri, who founded it; Guinness recognizes it as the oldest continuously operating degree-granting institution.
When these universities were founded.Al-Azhar, Cairo: It began as a Cairo mosque, and became a leading center of Sunni Islamic learning.
When these universities were founded.Bologna: Students ran it early on, hiring and paying their professors; 'alma mater' comes from its motto.
When these universities were founded.Paris: Its medieval theology school drew scholars; the Sorbonne is named for Robert de Sorbon, who founded a college there in 1257.
When these universities were founded.Cambridge: Scholars left Oxford after a dispute with townspeople and settled here in 1209.
When these universities were founded.Coimbra: It began in Lisbon in 1290 and moved to Coimbra for good in 1537, and its old library is lined with gilded wood.
When these universities were founded.Charles University, Prague: Founded by Emperor Charles IV, it is the oldest university in the Czech Republic and Central Europe.
When these universities were founded.Heidelberg: Germany's oldest university, it kept a student jail where rowdy students were locked up as a punishment.
When these universities were founded.St Andrews: Scotland's oldest university, and where Prince William met Kate Middleton.
When these universities were founded.Uppsala: Sweden's oldest university, where astronomer Anders Celsius taught; he proposed the temperature scale named after him.

Heavier things around the house.US stick of butter: A US stick is four ounces, and the wrapper is marked in tablespoons for easy cutting.
Heavier things around the house.Full can of soda: Regular cans sink in water while diet cans float, because of the sugar's density.
Heavier things around the house.Full wine bottle: The glass bottle itself weighs around 500 g, over a third of the total.
Heavier things around the house.Gallon of milk: A US gallon of water weighs about 3.8 kg, and milk is a touch heavier.
Heavier things around the house.Heaviest bowling ball: The maximum allowed weight is 16 pounds, set by the sport's governing body.
Heavier things around the house.Full 20-lb propane tank: The '20 lb' refers to the propane inside; add the steel tank, and you reach nearly 17 kg.
Heavier things around the house.UK bag of cement: UK bags are 25 kg because of manual handling rules, and Portland cement was patented in 1824.
Heavier things around the house.Washing machine: Concrete blocks are often used inside as counterweights to stop it dancing across the floor.
Heavier things around the house.Upright piano: Its cast iron frame bears many tonnes of string tension, so it is far from fragile.
Heavier things around the house.Family car: Cars have grown heavier over decades because of safety features, and this is far more than a butter stick.

Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Born Cassius Clay: Ali was named after Cassius Marcellus Clay, a Kentucky abolitionist who was also the namesake of his father.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Olympic gold in Rome: He won light heavyweight gold at the 1960 Rome Olympics; a replacement medal was given to him at Atlanta in 1996.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Beats Sonny Liston: He won the heavyweight title at 22 by beating Sonny Liston, then announced his new name after joining the Nation of Islam.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Refuses the draft: He was stripped of his title and banned from boxing for over three years, until the Supreme Court cleared him in 1971.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Loses to Joe Frazier: The 1971 bout with Frazier at Madison Square Garden was billed the Fight of the Century, and Frazier won on points.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Rumble in the Jungle: The Rumble in the Jungle in Kinshasa saw him beat George Foreman with his rope-a-dope tactic.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Thrilla in Manila: The Thrilla in Manila was his third fight with Frazier, and he called it the closest thing to dying.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Last fight: His last fight was a loss to Trevor Berbick in 1981, ending a career of 56 wins and 5 losses.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Lights the Olympic flame: He lit the cauldron at Atlanta 1996 with trembling hands because of Parkinson's, which made it one of the Games' most moving moments.
Muhammad Ali's life, in order.Dies: He died in Scottsdale, Arizona, aged 74, and his funeral was held in his home city of Louisville.
